description: The schemas as the specification writes the one point our proposal changes: a country code is any string, as the row types it, compared by exact equality, since the codes "ISO-3166-3" names are of countries that no longer exist. Every point the text leaves open is filled as in the schemas we propose.

switches.proposed: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code, such as `USA`, as OpenRTB 2.6 writes `geo.country`, checked against the codes ISO 3166-1 assigns.
switches.question: What is a country code in `countries`, which the text writes as "ISO-3166-3"?
switches.reads: Each of a deal's `countries` is any string, as the row types it, a code a receiver compares by exact equality, with no check that ISO 3166-1 assigns it.
switches.written: Any string, as the row types it: the codes ISO 3166-3 names are the four-letter codes of countries that no longer exist, which no current deal can run in, so the row's string type is all that stays.
